newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends firm, end-users battle speculator.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends firm, end-users battle speculator.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended higher on Thursday in what most industry sources described as a battle between end-users looking at adequate supply and traders zeroing in on firm crude futures and arbitrage interest to the States.
"There is enough supply now on the cargo side. I don't see anyone who needs a cargo," said one end-user. "It's getting pushed up by the swaps."
Dec swaps ended $2 higher at $232/$233 while cargoes, based on the backwardation, were notionally valued at $232/$234 cif, though no trades were heard at this level.

Bullish traders pointed to firm propane in the U.S., which hit seven-year highs this week in the Midcontinent, sharply higher crude oil futures, and talk that there was still interest to send material to the U.S.

The end-user claimed at least two to three small parcels of about 5,000 tonnes were available for German paraffinic material. He also said a Russian cargo on offer this week in NWE ended up in tankage.
He also argued that if crude prices show any sign of retreating, naphtha will also drop sharply with 12 stems expected to load of Algeria's Skikda port in December.
The naphtha to crude crack spread is also overvalued by about $6-$8 based on naphtha's fundamentals, he said.
